proposals.motivation: Both LiF (0.310 eV, bin 15) and Li2O (0.337 eV, bin 16) gave reaction products with the sulfide, and Li3PO4 was much worse (1.82 eV). A halide with a non-fluoride anion that matches the electrolyte's Cl may reduce the contact penalty further.

proposal.hypothesis: Li6Ti2O7 is the Ti analogue of Li6Zr2O7, the best oxide so far (penalty 0.189 eV, bin 9). It is a Li-rich, wide-gap oxide with only Ti4+ as its non-Li cation, and the Li-rich, low non-Li-fraction trend that lowered the penalty for Li2O and Li6Zr2O7 should carry over. Ti4+ may be somewhat more reducible than Zr4+, so this tests whether the Ti framework keeps the penalty low or raises it.
proposal.motivation: Li6Zr2O7 (bin 9) and Li2O (bin 9) gave the lowest contact penalties, and Li6Zr2O7 is a Zr-oxide Li-rich framework. The Ti analogue Li6Ti2O7 is the closest untested member of that family.

proposal.hypothesis: Li5Al(SiO4)2 is a Li-rich oxosilicate whose only non-Li cations are Al3+ and Si4+, both hard to reduce. The high Li/cation ratio and robust tetrahedral framework should limit sulfide-driven redox and anion exchange, in line with the low-penalty Li2O and Li6Zr2O7 contacts. It tests whether a mixed Al/Si Li-rich oxide can reach the bin-9 level with a different cation set.
proposal.motivation: Li2O and Li6Zr2O7 gave the lowest penalties (bin 9). Li-rich oxides with robust, hard-to-reduce high-valence cations performed best, while Li8SiO6 and Li3BO3 did worse, so a Li-rich Al/Si oxide is a reasonable next test.
